regular treatment with the long acting beta-2 agonist salmeterol for 1 week significantly diminished the protection against methacholine bronchoconstriction conferred by albutreol, both with bodesonide and with placeo.

regular use of a long- acting beta 2- agonist, such as salmeterol, causes a progressive loss of bronchoprotective effects of albuterorl, and that this loss of bronchoprotein occurs even when a high dose of inhaled glucocorricoids, such as budesonide, is used.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of in vitro and in vivo glucocorticoids on the development of tolerance in vitro and in the lung to beta-agonists and the role of beta 2-adrenergic receptors.
the development of tolerance and the mechanisms underlying tolerance to the bronchodilator and bronchoprotective effects of inhaled long-acting beta-2 agonists in asthma.
the effect of in- and exhaled breath condensate (EBC) on the development of tolerance in asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inhaled glucocoritoids do not prevent beta 2-receptor down-regulation, and that beta 2-recepter down-regulation occurs in the presence and absence of glucocorticoid.
inhaled glucocortiocoid does not prevent the loss of protection against bronchoconstriction by long acting beta agonist.
the use of a high dose of inhaled glucocortioid does not prevent the tolerance to the broncho-protective effect of long-acting in-haled beta-2-agonists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhaled budesonic (800 micrograms) twice daily did not prevent tolerance to bronchoprotection conferred by salmeterol in asthmatic subjects.
regular use of a long acting beta 2- agonist (LABA) can cause a tolerance to the protection against bronchoconstriction conferred by a short acting beta 2 agonist.
the use of a high dose of inhaled corticosteroids does not protect against the tolerance to the bronchodilatory effect of beta 2- agonists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of inhaled glucocortocoids does not prevent the development of tolerance in patients with asthma.
the loss of protection is not prevented by the inhaled glucocortoid.
the regular use of beta agonists, even at low dose, is not without risks, and the use of these drugs should be carefully monitored.
